clue.text: Taken to court in SW19 for fraud following game

indicators.note: the fraud word comes after the game word, so its letters are placed second

parts.note: tennis is a game
a racket is a fraudulent scheme or scam

explanation.surface: Someone is prosecuted at Wimbledon for a swindle after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: SW19 is the London postcode of Wimbledon, home of the famous tennis championships; 'taken to court' sounds legal but means carried onto a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A player carries this bat-like strung frame onto the grass courts at Wimbledon.

clue.text: English, slim, golden girl

parts.note: lean means slim
or is the heraldic word for gold or golden

explanation.surface: A slender, fair-haired English young woman is described.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic term for gold, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Those ran adrift in this part of the Atlantic

indicators.note: drifting loose, the letters of these two words wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors who drifted off course found themselves in some stretch of ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adrift' rearranges THOSE RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea between Britain and Scandinavia is an arm of the Atlantic Ocean.

clue.text: The end of promenades plus what's on the beach

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: and means plus

explanation.surface: Seaside walkways finish where the shore begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine grains covering the seashore.

clue.text: Basic act or specially arranged display of tumbling perhaps

indicators.note: arranged in a special way, the letters of these words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A simple routine, put together carefully, could make a show of somersaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially arranged' rearranges BASIC ACT OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnastic feats such as tumbling performed as a show; tumbling is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Jack can be a rogue at the bridge table

explanation.surface: At the card table the jack might turn out to be a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games such as bridge the jack is also called the knave; separately the word means a dishonest man.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack is the old name for the court card below the queen, and a scoundrel is an old word for a dishonest rascal.

clue.text: He tries to persuade part-time help to exercise restraint initially

parts.note: a temp is a temporary or part-time worker

indicators.note: the opening letters of the three words that precede it are taken

explanation.surface: A temporary assistant is urged to hold back from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'to exercise restraint', giving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who entices or lures someone into doing something.

clue.text: Pay cost of dance shoes worn by Shearer?

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay its cost
a ball is a formal dance
boots are a kind of footwear

explanation.surface: Who pays for the dancing shoes of a famous footballer?
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a famous English footballer, England's captain in the late 1990s; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The studded footwear a soccer player such as Shearer wears on the pitch.

clue.text: Drug route trail leads to motorcycle stadium

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a way is a route
a track is a trail or path

explanation.surface: A path used for drug trafficking ends at a racing venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirt oval where motorbikes race on a short circuit.

clue.text: Go on too long about cricket score

parts.note: over can mean about, as in 'a row over money'
a run is the basic unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket innings drags past its scheduled time.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run is a single point scored by the batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed the allotted time or limit.

clue.text: When transporting a pram do find guide for drivers

indicators.note: carrying something about shifts its position, so these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: When wheeling a baby carriage, look for directions for motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transporting' rearranges A PRAM DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart of highways a motorist consults to navigate.

clue.text: Fish using net rejected by companion

indicators.note: thrown back, the word net is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A companion turns down a net used to catch a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns NET into TEN; CH stands for Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater carp-family species found in European ponds.

clue.text: One missing tea's been upset

indicators.note: an upset cup has its contents thrown about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is absent because the tea tray has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges TEAS BEEN; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is not present where expected.

clue.text: Fellow always takes a wicket in a state of high excitement

parts.note: ever means always
in cricket the wicket is also the pitch, the strip between the stumps

explanation.surface: A man who keeps taking cricket wickets is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket 'wicket' can mean the playing strip, also called the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a peak of frenzied enthusiasm.

clue.text: Deals with contracts

explanation.surface: Someone handles legal paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Both deals and contracts are settled arrangements between parties.

clue.text: Tie down initially then fight back

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word down is taken
the word for fight is read in reverse

parts.note: war means fight

explanation.surface: A match ends level after an early setback and a counter-attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns WAR into RAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A game that ends level with neither side winning.

clue.text: Scholarly people illuminated the period and uplifted it

parts.note: lit means illuminated
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up a word reads it from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Learned folk brightened their age and raised its spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uplifted' reverses IT to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated, literary intellectuals as a class.

clue.text: See work put into skater's jump

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Watch the effort that goes into a figure skater's leap.
explanation.walkthrough: LO ('lo and behold') means see; OP (opus) is a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure-skating jump taking off and landing on the same edge.

clue.text: What top batsmen should be doing for a chance of promotion?

definitions.text: What top batsmen should be doing

explanation.surface: A question about the best batsmen in a cricket team and career advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the first two batsmen in the order are the 'openers', who start the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading off the batting in cricket, and a vacancy offering a job opportunity.

clue.text: Move swiftly to grab something printed in a charming way

indicators.note: grabbing something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to fly is to move swiftly
an etching is a print made from an etched plate

explanation.surface: Someone dashes to seize a printed item gracefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractively, in a pleasing and appealing manner.

clue.text: Go on a diet specially arranged for plant in the Borders

indicators.note: arranged in a special way, these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone starts a carefully planned diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially arranged' rearranges GO A DIET, with 'on' a link; the Scottish Borders is a region of south-east Scotland, local colour from the setter Highlander.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy annual flower grown in gardens, including those of the Scottish Borders.

clue.text: Coincides in part with completed track circuits

parts.note: something over is finished or completed
laps are circuits of a track

explanation.surface: A race where finished laps partly match.
explanation.definitionFit: Extends partly over the same area or time as something else.

clue.text: The only solution containing an antiseptic

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letters within it, running across the words

explanation.surface: The sole liquid remedy holds a germ-killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'onLY SOLution'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of disinfectant liquid used to kill germs.

clue.text: Duck that is back on the German river

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed before the next piece
the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is
der is the German for the

explanation.surface: A duck returns to sit on a river in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IE into EI; the Eider is also a river in northern Germany, so 'river' adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea duck prized for its soft down.

clue.text: Old style of writing competition for all comers

parts.note: a person's pen is their style of writing, as in 'a witty pen'

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned script is used in a public contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament in which amateurs and professionals alike may enter, such as a golf championship.

clue.text: What ladies sometimes wear in doubles starts to enliven tennis

parts.note: twins are doubles of each other

indicators.note: the opening letters of the following two words are taken

explanation.surface: Women's doubles players bring some liveliness to the tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes E and T from 'enliven tennis'.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching cardigan and jumper (sweater) worn together.

clue.text: Credit cards use most recent photograph around

indicators.note: the photograph word goes around the other

parts.note: pic is short for picture or photograph
last means most recent

explanation.surface: Bank cards carry a recent photo of the holder.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective slang for payment cards made of polymer.

clue.text: Player's rating as a club user a disadvantage after the game?

definitions.text: Player's rating as a club user

indicators.note: the disadvantage word comes after the game word

parts.note: golf is the game played with clubs
a handicap is a disadvantage

explanation.surface: A player's grade at the club may be a drawback once the match ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club user' sounds like a member of a social club but means someone wielding golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A number measuring a golfer's ability, used to equalise matches.
